# PSXRecompStudio

> Open-source PlayStation 1 research project for PS1/PSX binary analysis, MIPS R3000A validation, static recompilation, and native-porting experiments.

PSXRecompStudio is a research platform, not a claim of complete commercial-game compatibility. It can analyze legal user-supplied PS-X EXE and supported CHD inputs, validate bounded real-ROM-derived recompilation paths, build runnable generated-host artifacts, and produce classified headless execution results.

## Current capabilities

- PS-X EXE and supported CHD analysis.
- MIPS R3000A decode, execution, delay-slot, exception, interrupt, and differential validation.
- Static recompilation research with deterministic host-code generation and bounded real-ROM-derived proofs.
- Headless `psxrecomp recompile` and `psxrecomp run` workflows with JSON and privacy-safe diagnostic reports.
- Partial BIOS HLE and PS1 Runtime hardware models.
- Mixed C#/.NET application code and C++/Rust native implementation behind a stable C ABI.

## Important limitations

- Complete commercial PS1 titles are not yet recompiled into finished native ports.
- BIOS HLE coverage is partial.
- GPU production integration is incomplete.
- SPU audio behavior, CD-ROM, MDEC, GTE, and other hardware behavior remain incomplete or evidence-gated.

## Content and legal policy

The repository does not distribute copyrighted ROM, ISO, CHD, BIOS/firmware, commercial game executable, or extracted game-asset content. Users are responsible for supplying legally obtained inputs and for complying with applicable law and license terms.

The public site is intentionally available in English and Japanese for the core Home/FAQ/CLI/Runtime search intents. The linked HTML pages and repository documentation are authoritative; this file is only a supplemental navigation summary.
